# pest - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pest/^2/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#pest-the-elegant-parser)pest. The Elegant Parser

pest is a general purpose parser written in Rust with a focus on accessibility, correctness,
and performance. It uses parsing expression grammars (or [PEG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parsing_expression_grammar)) as input, which are similar in
spirit to regular expressions, but which offer the enhanced expressivity needed to parse
complex languages.

[§](https://docs.rs#getting-started)Getting started

The recommended way to start parsing with pest is to read the official [book](https://pest.rs/book).

Other helpful resources:

- API reference on [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/pest)
- play with grammars and share them on our [fiddle](https://pest.rs/#editor)
- find previous common questions answered or ask questions on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/pest-parser/pest/discussions)
- leave feedback, ask questions, or greet us on [Gitter](https://gitter.im/pest-parser/pest)or[Discord](https://discord.gg/XEGACtWpT2)

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

The core of pest is the trait [ Parser](https://docs.rs/trait.Parser.html), which provides an interface to the parsing
functionality.

The accompanying crate `pest_derive` can automatically generate a [ Parser](https://docs.rs/trait.Parser.html) from a PEG
grammar. Using

`pest_derive` is highly encouraged, but it is also possible to implement
[manually if required.](https://docs.rs/trait.Parser.html)

`Parser`[§](https://docs.rs#pest-files)`.pest` files

Grammar definitions reside in custom `.pest` files located in the crate `src` directory.
Parsers are automatically generated from these files using `#[derive(Parser)]` and a special
`#[grammar = "..."]` attribute on a dummy struct.

The syntax of `.pest` files is documented in the [ pest_derive crate](https://docs.rs/pest_derive/).

[§](https://docs.rs#inline-grammars)Inline grammars

Grammars can also be inlined by using the `#[grammar_inline = "..."]` attribute.

[§](https://docs.rs#grammar)Grammar

A grammar is a series of rules separated by whitespace, possibly containing comments.

[§](https://docs.rs#comments)Comments

Comments start with `//` and end at the end of the line.

`// a comment`[§](https://docs.rs#rules)Rules

Rules have the following form:

The name of the rule is formed from alphanumeric characters or `_` with the condition that the
first character is not a digit and is used to create token pairs. When the rule starts being
parsed, the starting part of the token is being produced, with the ending part being produced
when the rule finishes parsing.

The following token pair notation `a(b(), c())` denotes the tokens: start `a`, start `b`, end
`b`, start `c`, end `c`, end `a`.

[§](https://docs.rs#modifiers)Modifiers

Modifiers are optional and can be one of `_`, `@`, `$`, or `!`. These modifiers change the
behavior of the rules.

-
Silent ( `_`)Silent rules do not create token pairs during parsing, nor are they error-reported. Parsing `"ab"`produces the token pair`b()`.
-
Atomic ( `@`)Atomic rules do not accept whitespace or comments within their expressions and have a cascading effect on any rule they call. I.e. rules that are not atomic but are called by atomic rules behave atomically. Any rules called by atomic rules do not generate token pairs. Parsing `"ab"`produces the token pair`b()`, while`"a b"`produces an error.
-
Compound-atomic ( `$`)Compound-atomic are identical to atomic rules with the exception that rules called by them are not forbidden from generating token pairs. Parsing `"ab"`produces the token pairs`b(a())`, while`"a b"`produces an error.
-
Non-atomic ( `!`)Non-atomic are identical to normal rules with the exception that they stop the cascading effect of atomic and compound-atomic rules. Parsing both `"ab"`and`"a b"`produce the token pairs`c(a())`.

[§](https://docs.rs#expressions)Expressions

Expressions can be either terminals or non-terminals.

- Terminals

| Terminal | Usage |
|---|---|
| `"a"` | matches the exact string `"a"` |
| `^"a"` | matches the exact string `"a"`case insensitively (ASCII only) |
| `'a'..'z'` | matches one character between `'a'`and`'z'` |
| `a` | matches rule `a` |

Strings and characters follow
[Rust’s escape mechanisms](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/tokens.html#byte-escapes), while
identifiers can contain alphanumeric characters and underscores (`_`), as long as they do not
start with a digit.

- Non-terminals

| Non-terminal | Usage |
|---|---|
| `(e)` | matches `e` |
| `e1 ~ e2` | matches the sequence `e1``e2` |
| `e1 | e2` | matches either `e1`or`e2` |
| `e*` | matches `e`zero or more times |
| `e+` | matches `e`one or more times |
| `e{n}` | matches `e`exactly`n`times |
| `e{, n}` | matches `e`at most`n`times |
| `e{n,}` | matches `e`at least`n`times |
| `e{m, n}` | matches `e`between`m`and`n`times inclusively |
| `e?` | optionally matches `e` |
| `&e` | matches `e`without making progress |
| `!e` | matches if `e`doesn’t match without making progress |
| `PUSH(e)` | matches `e`and pushes it’s captured string down the stack |

where `e`, `e1`, and `e2` are expressions.

Matching is greedy, without backtracking. Note the difference in behavior for these two rules in matching identifiers that don’t end in an underscore:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// input: ab_bb_b
identifier = @{ "a" ~ ("b"|"_")* ~ "b" }
// matches:      a     b_bb_b       nothing -> error!
identifier = @{ "a" ~ ("_"* ~ "b")* }
// matches:      a     b, _bb, _b   in three repetitions
```
Expressions can modify the stack only if they match the input. For example,
if `e1` in the compound expression `e1 | e2` does not match the input, then
it does not modify the stack, so `e2` sees the stack in the same state as
`e1` did. Repetitions and optionals (`e*`, `e+`, `e{, n}`, `e{n,}`,
`e{m,n}`, `e?`) can modify the stack each time `e` matches. The `!e` and `&e`
expressions are a special case; they never modify the stack.
Many languages have “keyword” tokens (e.g. if, for, while) as well as general
tokens (e.g. identifier) that matches any word. In order to match a keyword,
generally, you may need to restrict that is not immediately followed by another
letter or digit (otherwise it would be matched as an identifier).

[§](https://docs.rs#special-rules)Special rules

Special rules can be called within the grammar. They are:

- `WHITESPACE`- runs between rules and sub-rules
- `COMMENT`- runs between rules and sub-rules
- `ANY`- matches exactly one- `char`
- `SOI`- (start-of-input) matches only when a- `Parser`is still at the starting position
- `EOI`- (end-of-input) matches only when a- `Parser`has reached its end
- `PUSH`- matches a string and pushes it to the stack
- `PUSH_LITERAL`- pushes a literal string to the stack
- `POP`- pops a string from the stack and matches it
- `POP_ALL`- pops the entire state of the stack and matches it
- `PEEK`- peeks a string from the stack and matches it
- `PEEK[a..b]`- peeks part of the stack and matches it
- `PEEK_ALL`- peeks the entire state of the stack and matches it
- `DROP`- drops the top of the stack (fails to match if the stack is empty)

`WHITESPACE` and `COMMENT` should be defined manually if needed. All other rules cannot be
overridden.

[§](https://docs.rs#whitespace-and-comment)`WHITESPACE` and `COMMENT`

When defined, these rules get matched automatically in sequences (`~`) and repetitions
(`*`, `+`) between expressions. Atomic rules and those rules called by atomic rules are exempt
from this behavior.

These rules should be defined so as to match one whitespace character and one comment only since they are run in repetitions.

If both `WHITESPACE` and `COMMENT` are defined, this grammar:

is effectively transformed into this one behind the scenes:

[§](https://docs.rs#push-push_literal-pop-drop-and-peek)`PUSH`, `PUSH_LITERAL`, `POP`, `DROP`, and `PEEK`

`PUSH(e)` simply pushes the captured string of the expression `e` down a stack. This stack can
then later be used to match grammar based on its content with `POP` and `PEEK`.

`PUSH_LITERAL("a")` pushes the argument to the stack without considering the input. The
argument must be a literal string. This is often useful in conjunction with another rule before
it. For example, `"[" ~ PUSH_LITERAL("]")` will look for an opening bracket `[` and, if it
finds one, will push a closing bracket `]` to the stack. **Note**: `PUSH_LITERAL` requires the
`grammar-extras` feature to be enabled.

`PEEK` always matches the string at the top of stack. So, if the stack contains `["b", "a"]`
(`"a"` being on top), this grammar:

is effectively transformed into at parse time:

`POP` works the same way with the exception that it pops the string off of the stack if the
match worked. With the stack from above, if `POP` matches `"a"`, the stack will be mutated
to `["b"]`.

`DROP` makes it possible to remove the string at the top of the stack
without matching it. If the stack is nonempty, `DROP` drops the top of the
stack. If the stack is empty, then `DROP` fails to match.

[§](https://docs.rs#advanced-peeking)Advanced peeking

`PEEK[start..end]` and `PEEK_ALL` allow to peek deeper into the stack. The syntax works exactly
like Rust’s exclusive slice syntax. Additionally, negative indices can be used to indicate an
offset from the top. If the end lies before or at the start, the expression matches (as does
a `PEEK_ALL` on an empty stack). With the stack `["c", "b", "a"]` (`"a"` on top):

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
fill = PUSH("c") ~ PUSH("b") ~ PUSH("a")
v = { PEEK_ALL } = { "a" ~ "b" ~ "c" }  // top to bottom
w = { PEEK[..] } = { "c" ~ "b" ~ "a" }  // bottom to top
x = { PEEK[1..2] } = { PEEK[1..-1] } = { "b" }
y = { PEEK[..-2] } = { PEEK[0..1] } = { "a" }
z = { PEEK[1..] } = { PEEK[-2..3] } = { "c" ~ "b" }
n = { PEEK[2..-2] } = { PEEK[2..1] } = { "" }
```
For historical reasons, `PEEK_ALL` matches from top to bottom, while `PEEK[start..end]` matches
from bottom to top. There is currently no syntax to match a slice of the stack top to bottom.

[§](https://docs.rs#rule)`Rule`

All rules defined or used in the grammar populate a generated `enum` called `Rule`. This
implements `pest`’s `RuleType` and can be used throughout the API.

[§](https://docs.rs#built-in-rules)`Built-in rules`

Pest also comes with a number of built-in rules for convenience. They are:

- `ASCII_DIGIT`- matches a numeric character from 0..9
- `ASCII_NONZERO_DIGIT`- matches a numeric character from 1..9
- `ASCII_BIN_DIGIT`- matches a numeric character from 0..1
- `ASCII_OCT_DIGIT`- matches a numeric character from 0..7
- `ASCII_HEX_DIGIT`- matches a numeric character from 0..9 or a..f or A..F
- `ASCII_ALPHA_LOWER`- matches a character from a..z
- `ASCII_ALPHA_UPPER`- matches a character from A..Z
- `ASCII_ALPHA`- matches a character from a..z or A..Z
- `ASCII_ALPHANUMERIC`- matches a character from a..z or A..Z or 0..9
- `ASCII`- matches a character from \x00..\x7f
- `NEWLINE`- matches either “\n” or “\r\n” or “\r”

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Types for different kinds of parsing failures.
- [iterators](https://docs.rs/iterators/index.html)
- Types and iterators for parser output.
- [pratt_](https://docs.rs/pratt_parser/index.html)- parser
- Constructs useful in prefix, postfix, and infix operator parsing with the Pratt parsing method.
- [prec_](https://docs.rs/prec_climber/index.html)- climber - Deprecated
- Constructs useful in infix operator parsing with the precedence climbing method.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [fails_](https://docs.rs/macro.fails_with.html)- with
- Testing tool that compares produced errors.
- [parses_](https://docs.rs/macro.parses_to.html)- to
- Testing tool that compares produced tokens.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Lines](https://docs.rs/struct.Lines.html)
- Line iterator for Spans, created by `Span::lines()`
- [Lines](https://docs.rs/struct.LinesSpan.html)- Span
- Line iterator for Spans, created by `Span::lines_span()`
- [Parser](https://docs.rs/struct.ParserState.html)- State
- The complete state of a `Parser`
- [Position](https://docs.rs/struct.Position.html)
- A cursor position in a `&str`which provides useful methods to manually parse that string.
- [Span](https://docs.rs/struct.Span.html)
- A span over a `&str`. It is created from either[two](https://docs.rs/struct.Position.html#method.span)or from a`Position`s`Pair`
- [Stack](https://docs.rs/struct.Stack.html)
- Implementation of a `Stack`which maintains popped elements and length of previous states in order to rewind the stack to a previous state.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Atomicity](https://docs.rs/enum.Atomicity.html)
- The current atomicity of a `ParserState`
- [Lookahead](https://docs.rs/enum.Lookahead.html)
- The current lookahead status of a `ParserState`
- [Match](https://docs.rs/enum.MatchDir.html)- Dir
- Match direction for the stack. Used in `PEEK[a..b]`/`stack_match_peek_slice`.
- [Token](https://docs.rs/enum.Token.html)
- A token generated by a `Parser`.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Parser](https://docs.rs/trait.Parser.html)
- A trait with a single method that parses strings.
- [Rule](https://docs.rs/trait.RuleType.html)- Type
- A trait which parser rules must implement.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [merge_](https://docs.rs/fn.merge_spans.html)- spans
- Merges two spans into one.
- [set_](https://docs.rs/fn.set_call_limit.html)- call_ - limit
- Sets the maximum call limit for the parser state to prevent stack overflows or excessive execution times in some grammars. If set, the calls are tracked as a running total over all non-terminal rules that can nest closures (which are passed to transform the parser state).
- [set_](https://docs.rs/fn.set_error_detail.html)- error_ - detail
- Sets whether information for more error details should be collected. This is useful for debugging parser errors (as it leads to more comprehensive error messages), but it has a higher performance cost. (hence, it’s off by default)
- [state](https://docs.rs/fn.state.html)
- Creates a `ParserState`from a`&str`, supplying it to a closure`f`.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Parse](https://docs.rs/type.ParseResult.html)- Result
- Type alias to simplify specifying the return value of chained closures.

# pest_derive - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pest_derive/^2/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#pest-the-elegant-parser)pest. The Elegant Parser

pest is a general purpose parser written in Rust with a focus on accessibility, correctness,
and performance. It uses parsing expression grammars (or [PEG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parsing_expression_grammar)) as input, which are similar in
spirit to regular expressions, but which offer the enhanced expressivity needed to parse
complex languages.

[§](https://docs.rs#getting-started)Getting started

The recommended way to start parsing with pest is to read the official [book](https://pest.rs/book).

Other helpful resources:

- API reference on [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/pest)
- play with grammars and share them on our [fiddle](https://pest.rs/#editor)
- find previous common questions answered or ask questions on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/pest-parser/pest/discussions)
- leave feedback, ask questions, or greet us on [Gitter](https://gitter.im/pest-parser/pest)or[Discord](https://discord.gg/XEGACtWpT2)

[§](https://docs.rs#pest-files)`.pest` files

Grammar definitions reside in custom `.pest` files located in the `src` directory. Their path is
relative to `src` and is specified between the `derive` attribute and empty `struct` that
`Parser` will be derived on.

[§](https://docs.rs#inline-grammars)Inline grammars

Grammars can also be inlined by using the `#[grammar_inline = "..."]` attribute.

[§](https://docs.rs#grammar)Grammar

A grammar is a series of rules separated by whitespace, possibly containing comments.

[§](https://docs.rs#comments)Comments

Comments start with `//` and end at the end of the line.

`// a comment`[§](https://docs.rs#rules)Rules

Rules have the following form:

The name of the rule is formed from alphanumeric characters or `_` with the condition that the
first character is not a digit and is used to create token pairs. When the rule starts being
parsed, the starting part of the token is being produced, with the ending part being produced
when the rule finishes parsing.

The following token pair notation `a(b(), c())` denotes the tokens: start `a`, start `b`, end
`b`, start `c`, end `c`, end `a`.

[§](https://docs.rs#modifiers)Modifiers

Modifiers are optional and can be one of `_`, `@`, `$`, or `!`. These modifiers change the
behavior of the rules.

-
Silent ( `_`)Silent rules do not create token pairs during parsing, nor are they error-reported. Parsing `"ab"`produces the token pair`b()`.
-

| `'a'..'z'` | matches one character between `'a'`and`'z'` |

- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_time_literal.html)- time_ - literal
- 単独の時刻リテラル文字列を `ast::TimeValue`

# tdsl_parser - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tdsl-parser/1.23.0/tdsl_parser/index.html

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use error::`- [ParseDiagnostic](https://docs.rs/error/struct.ParseDiagnostic.html);
- `pub use error::`- [byte_offset_to_line_col](https://docs.rs/error/fn.byte_offset_to_line_col.html);
- `pub use format::`- [format_file](https://docs.rs/format/fn.format_file.html);
- `pub use format::`- [format_source](https://docs.rs/format/fn.format_source.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [ast](https://docs.rs/ast/index.html)
- [builder](https://docs.rs/builder/index.html)
- [comments](https://docs.rs/comments/index.html)
- DSL ソースからコメントを byte span 付きで収集する独立パス。
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- [format](https://docs.rs/format/index.html)
- AST → DSL ソース再 emit（フォーマッタ）。
- [now](https://docs.rs/now/index.html)
- Wall-clock “current year” resolution for the `now`keyword (#550).

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [parse](https://docs.rs/fn.parse.html)
- Parse a DSL source string into an AST `ast::File`
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_time_literal.html)- time_ - literal
- 単独の時刻リテラル文字列を `ast::TimeValue`

[14](#14)#[derive(Parser)]
[15](#15)#[grammar = "grammar.pest"]
[16](#16)struct TdslParser;
[17](#17)
[18](#18)pub fn parse(source: &str) -> Result<ast::File, error::ParseError> {
[20](#20)    let pairs = TdslParser::parse(Rule::file, source)?;
[21](#21)    let mut file = builder::build_file(pairs)?;
[22](#22)    file.comments = comments::scan_comments(source);
[24](#24)    Ok(file)
[25](#25)}
[26](#26)
[27](#27)pub fn parse_time_literal(s: &str) -> Result<ast::TimeValue, error::ParseError> {
[34](#34)    let trimmed = s.trim();
[35](#35)    let mut pairs = TdslParser::parse(Rule::time_literal_only, trimmed)?;
[36](#36)    let outer = pairs
[37](#37)        .next()
[38](#38)        .ok_or_else(|| error::ParseError::UnexpectedRule {
[39](#39)            rule: "time_literal_only: empty".to_string(),
[40](#40)            location: "0:0".to_string(),
[41](#41)        })?;
[42](#42)    let time_value_pair = outer
[43](#43)        .into_inner()
[44](#44)        .find(|p| matches!(p.as_rule(), Rule::time_value))
[45](#45)        .ok_or_else(|| error::ParseError::UnexpectedRule {
[46](#46)            rule: "time_literal_only: missing time_value".to_string(),
[47](#47)            location: "0:0".to_string(),
[48](#48)        })?;
[49](#49)    builder::parse_time_value(time_value_pair)
[50](#50)}

[56](#56)    #[test]
[57](#57)    fn parse_timeline_block() {
[58](#58)        let src = r#"
[59](#59)            timeline "中国王朝年表" {
[60](#60)                title "中国王朝年表";
[61](#61)                unit year;
[62](#62)                range -500..2000;
[63](#63)                calendar proleptic_gregorian;
[64](#64)            }
[65](#65)        "#;
[66](#66)        let file = parse(src).unwrap();
[67](#67)        assert_eq!(file.statements.len(), 1);
[68](#68)        match &file.statements[0].node {
[69](#69)            ast::Statement::Timeline(t) => {
[70](#70)                assert_eq!(t.name, "中国王朝年表");
[71](#71)                assert_eq!(t.title.as_deref(), Some("中国王朝年表"));
[72](#72)                assert_eq!(t.unit.as_deref(), Some("year"));
[73](#73)                assert_eq!(
[74](#74)                    t.range,
[75](#75)                    Some(ast::RangeExpr {
[76](#76)                        start: ast::TimeValue::Year(-500),
[77](#77)                        end: ast::TimeValue::Year(2000),
[78](#78)                    })
[79](#79)                );
[80](#80)                assert_eq!(t.calendar.as_deref(), Some("proleptic_gregorian"));
[81](#81)            }
[82](#82)            _ => panic!("expected Timeline"),
[83](#83)        }
[84](#84)    }

[87](#87)    fn parse_lane() {
[88](#88)        let src = r#"lane "漢" as han { kind dynasty; order 10; }"#;
[89](#89)        let file = parse(src).unwrap();
[90](#90)        assert_eq!(file.statements.len(), 1);
[91](#91)        match &file.statements[0].node {
[92](#92)            ast::Statement::Lane(l) => {
[93](#93)                assert_eq!(l.label, "漢");
[94](#94)                assert_eq!(l.alias.as_deref(), Some("han"));
[95](#95)                assert_eq!(l.kind.as_deref(), Some("dynasty"));
[96](#96)                assert_eq!(l.order, Some(10));
[97](#97)            }
[98](#98)            _ => panic!("expected Lane"),
[99](#99)        }
[100](#100)    }

[103](#103)    fn parse_span() {
[104](#104)        let src =
[105](#105)            r#"span han -206..220 "漢" { tags ["dynasty"]; source wd:Q7209; id "span:han"; };"#;
[106](#106)        let file = parse(src).unwrap();
[107](#107)        assert_eq!(file.statements.len(), 1);
[108](#108)        match &file.statements[0].node {
[109](#109)            ast::Statement::Span(s) => {
[110](#110)                assert_eq!(s.lane_ref, "han");
[111](#111)                assert_eq!(s.start, ast::TimeValue::Year(-206));
[112](#112)                assert_eq!(s.end, ast::TimeValue::Year(220));
[113](#113)                assert_eq!(s.label, "漢");
[114](#114)                assert_eq!(s.props.tags, vec!["dynasty"]);
[115](#115)                assert_eq!(
[116](#116)                    s.props.source,
[117](#117)                    Some(ast::SourceRef {
[118](#118)                        prefix: "wd".to_string(),
[119](#119)                        qid: "Q7209".to_string(),
[120](#120)                    })
[121](#121)                );
[122](#122)                assert_eq!(s.props.id.as_deref(), Some("span:han"));
[123](#123)            }
[124](#124)            _ => panic!("expected Span"),
[125](#125)        }
[126](#126)    }

[128](#128)    #[test]
[129](#129)    fn parse_span_open_ended_with_now() {
[130](#130)        let src = r#"span reiwa 2019..now "令和" {};"#;
[132](#132)        let file = parse(src).unwrap();
[133](#133)        match &file.statements[0].node {
[134](#134)            ast::Statement::Span(s) => {
[135](#135)                assert_eq!(s.start, ast::TimeValue::Year(2019));
[136](#136)                assert!(s.end_open, "end_open must be true when `now` is used");
[137](#137)                match s.end {
[138](#138)                    ast::TimeValue::Year(y) => {
[139](#139)                        assert!((2020..=2200).contains(&y), "unexpected resolved year: {y}");
[140](#140)                    }
[141](#141)                    other => panic!("expected Year, got {other:?}"),
[142](#142)                }
[143](#143)            }
[144](#144)            _ => panic!("expected Span"),
[145](#145)        }
[146](#146)    }

[206](#206)    #[test]
[207](#207)    fn parse_import_block() {
[208](#208)        let src = r#"
[209](#209)            import wikidata as wd {
[210](#210)                entity Q7209 as han_dynasty;
[211](#211)                query "SELECT ?item WHERE { ?item wdt:P31 wd:Q28171280 . }" as dynasties;
[212](#212)                policy merge_by_source;
[213](#213)            }
[214](#214)        "#;
[215](#215)        let file = parse(src).unwrap();
[216](#216)        assert_eq!(file.statements.len(), 1);
[217](#217)        match &file.statements[0].node {
[218](#218)            ast::Statement::Import(imp) => {
[219](#219)                assert_eq!(imp.source_type, "wikidata");
[220](#220)                assert_eq!(imp.alias.as_deref(), Some("wd"));
[221](#221)                assert_eq!(imp.items.len(), 2);
[222](#222)                assert!(matches!(
[223](#223)                    &imp.items[0],
[224](#224)                    ast::ImportItem::Entity { qid, alias }
[225](#225)                        if qid == "Q7209" && alias.as_deref() == Some("han_dynasty")
[226](#226)                ));
[227](#227)                assert!(matches!(
[228](#228)                    &imp.items[1],
[229](#229)                    ast::ImportItem::Query { query, alias }
[230](#230)                        if query.contains("P31") && alias.as_deref() == Some("dynasties")
[231](#231)                ));
[232](#232)                assert_eq!(imp.policy, Some(ast::ReimportPolicy::MergeBySource));
[233](#233)            }
[234](#234)            _ => panic!("expected Import"),
[235](#235)        }
[236](#236)    }

[260](#260)    #[test]
[261](#261)    fn parse_map_expr_with_fallback() {
[262](#262)        let src = r#"
[263](#263)            map wd.han to span {
[264](#264)                lane han;
[265](#265)                start claim(P580).year ?? claim(P571).year;
[266](#266)                end claim(P582).year ?? claim(P576).year;
[267](#267)                label label@ja ?? label@en;
[268](#268)            }
[269](#269)        "#;
[270](#270)        let file = parse(src).unwrap();
[271](#271)        match &file.statements[0].node {
[272](#272)            ast::Statement::Map(m) => {
[273](#273)                let start = m
[274](#274)                    .props
[275](#275)                    .iter()
[276](#276)                    .find_map(|p| match p {
[277](#277)                        ast::MapProp::Start(e) => Some(e),
[278](#278)                        _ => None,
[279](#279)                    })
[280](#280)                    .expect("start present");
[281](#281)                assert_eq!(start.fallbacks.len(), 2);
[282](#282)                match &start.fallbacks[0] {
[283](#283)                    ast::MapFallback::Claim(c) => {
[284](#284)                        assert_eq!(c.claim.property, "P580");
[285](#285)                        assert_eq!(c.accessor.as_deref(), Some("year"));
[286](#286)                    }
[287](#287)                    _ => panic!("expected Claim"),
[288](#288)                }
[289](#289)                match &start.fallbacks[1] {
[290](#290)                    ast::MapFallback::Claim(c) => {
[291](#291)                        assert_eq!(c.claim.property, "P571");
[292](#292)                        assert_eq!(c.accessor.as_deref(), Some("year"));
[293](#293)                    }
[294](#294)                    _ => panic!("expected Claim"),
[295](#295)                }
[296](#296)
[297](#297)                let end = m
[298](#298)                    .props
[299](#299)                    .iter()
[300](#300)                    .find_map(|p| match p {
[301](#301)                        ast::MapProp::End(e) => Some(e),
[302](#302)                        _ => None,
[303](#303)                    })
[304](#304)                    .expect("end present");
[305](#305)                assert_eq!(end.fallbacks.len(), 2);
[306](#306)                match &end.fallbacks[0] {
[307](#307)                    ast::MapFallback::Claim(c) => assert_eq!(c.claim.property, "P582"),
[308](#308)                    _ => panic!("expected Claim"),
[309](#309)                }
[310](#310)                match &end.fallbacks[1] {
[311](#311)                    ast::MapFallback::Claim(c) => assert_eq!(c.claim.property, "P576"),
[312](#312)                    _ => panic!("expected Claim"),
[313](#313)                }
[314](#314)            }
[315](#315)            _ => panic!("expected Map"),
[316](#316)        }
[317](#317)    }

[353](#353)    fn parse_map_expr_three_fallbacks() {
[354](#354)        let src = r#"
[355](#355)            map wd.x to event {
[356](#356)                lane a;
[357](#357)                time claim(P580).year ?? claim(P571).year ?? claim(P569).year;
[358](#358)                label label@ja;
[359](#359)            }
[360](#360)        "#;
[361](#361)        let file = parse(src).unwrap();
[362](#362)        match &file.statements[0].node {
[363](#363)            ast::Statement::Map(m) => {
[364](#364)                let time = m
[365](#365)                    .props
[366](#366)                    .iter()
[367](#367)                    .find_map(|p| match p {
[368](#368)                        ast::MapProp::Time(e) => Some(e),
[369](#369)                        _ => None,
[370](#370)                    })
[371](#371)                    .expect("time present");
[372](#372)                assert_eq!(time.fallbacks.len(), 3);
[373](#373)                for (fb, expected) in time.fallbacks.iter().zip(["P580", "P571", "P569"]) {
[374](#374)                    match fb {
[375](#375)                        ast::MapFallback::Claim(c) => assert_eq!(c.claim.property, expected),
[376](#376)                        _ => panic!("expected Claim"),
[377](#377)                    }
[378](#378)                }
[379](#379)            }
[380](#380)            _ => panic!("expected Map"),
[381](#381)        }
[382](#382)    }
[383](#383)
[384](#384)    fn extract_map_filters(file: &ast::File) -> Vec<ast::FilterExpr> {
[385](#385)        match &file.statements[0].node {
[386](#386)            ast::Statement::Map(m) => m
[387](#387)                .props
[388](#388)                .iter()
[389](#389)                .filter_map(|p| match p {
[390](#390)                    ast::MapProp::Filter(e) => Some(e.clone()),
[391](#391)                    _ => None,
[392](#392)                })
[393](#393)                .collect(),
[394](#394)            _ => panic!("expected Map"),
[395](#395)        }
[396](#396)    }

[398](#398)    #[test]
[399](#399)    fn parse_map_filter_basic_gt() {
[400](#400)        let src = r#"
[401](#401)            map wd.x to span {
[402](#402)                lane a;
[403](#403)                filter claim(P580).year > 1000;
[404](#404)                start claim(P580).year;
[405](#405)                end claim(P582).year;
[406](#406)                label label@ja;
[407](#407)            }
[408](#408)        "#;
[409](#409)        let file = parse(src).unwrap();
[410](#410)        let filters = extract_map_filters(&file);
[411](#411)        assert_eq!(filters.len(), 1);
[412](#412)        match &filters[0] {
[413](#413)            ast::FilterExpr::Compare { lhs, op, rhs } => {
[414](#414)                assert!(matches!(lhs, ast::FilterOperand::Claim(_)));
[415](#415)                assert_eq!(*op, ast::CompareOp::Gt);
[416](#416)                assert!(matches!(rhs, ast::FilterOperand::Int(1000)));
[417](#417)            }
[418](#418)            other => panic!("expected Compare, got {other:?}"),
[419](#419)        }
[420](#420)    }

[632](#632)    fn parse_full_example() {
[633](#633)        let src = r#"
[634](#634)            timeline "中国王朝年表" {
[635](#635)                title "中国王朝年表";
[636](#636)                unit year;
[637](#637)                range -500..2000;
[638](#638)                calendar proleptic_gregorian;
[639](#639)            }
[640](#640)
[641](#641)            lane "漢" as han { kind dynasty; order 10; }
[642](#642)            lane "秦" as qin { kind dynasty; order 20; }
[643](#643)
[644](#644)            span han -206..220 "漢" { tags ["dynasty"]; source wd:Q7209; id "span:han"; };
[645](#645)            span qin -221..-206 "秦" { tags ["dynasty"]; source wd:Q7462; id "span:qin"; };
[646](#646)
[647](#647)            event han -209 "陳勝・呉広の乱" {};
[648](#648)            event_range han 184..204 "黄巾の乱" { tags ["war"]; };
[649](#649)
[650](#650)            import wikidata as wd {
[651](#651)                entity Q7209 as han_dynasty;
[652](#652)                policy merge_by_source;
[653](#653)            }
[654](#654)
[655](#655)            map wd.han_dynasty to span {
[656](#656)                lane han;
[657](#657)                start claim(P571).year;
[658](#658)                end claim(P576).year;
[659](#659)                label label@ja ?? label@en;
[660](#660)            }
[661](#661)        "#;
[662](#662)        let file = parse(src).unwrap();
[663](#663)        assert_eq!(file.statements.len(), 9);
[665](#665)    }

[667](#667)    #[test]
[668](#668)    fn parse_unknown_target_type_fails() {
[669](#669)        let src = r#"
[670](#670)            map wd.x to unknown_type {
[671](#671)                lane a;
[672](#672)            }
[673](#673)        "#;
[674](#674)        let err = parse(src).expect_err("unknown target_type should fail to parse");
[675](#675)        assert!(
[676](#676)            matches!(&err, error::ParseError::UnknownTargetType(v) if v == "unknown_type"),
[677](#677)            "expected UnknownTargetType(\"unknown_type\"), got: {err:?}"
[678](#678)        );
[679](#679)        let msg = err.to_string();
[681](#681)        assert!(
[682](#682)            msg.contains("unknown_type")
[683](#683)                && msg.contains("span")
[684](#684)                && msg.contains("event")
[685](#685)                && msg.contains("event_range"),
[686](#686)            "error message should list the invalid value and all allowed types, got: {msg}"
[687](#687)        );
[688](#688)    }

[918](#918)        "#;

[920](#920)        assert_eq!(file.statements.len(), 1);
[921](#921)        match &file.statements[0].node {
[922](#922)            ast::Statement::Apply(a) => {
[923](#923)                assert_eq!(a.template_alias, "person_life");
[924](#924)                assert_eq!(a.import_alias, "emperors");
[925](#925)                assert_eq!(a.overrides.len(), 1);
[926](#926)                assert!(matches!(&a.overrides[0], ast::MapProp::Lane(id) if id == "imperial"));
[927](#927)            }
[928](#928)            _ => panic!("expected Apply"),
[929](#929)        }
[930](#930)    }

[1057](#1057)                    tags: merge;

[1059](#1059)            }
[1060](#1060)        "#;
[1061](#1061)        let result = parse(src);

[1063](#1063)        let file = result.unwrap();
[1064](#1064)        let import = match &file.statements[0].node {
[1065](#1065)            crate::ast::Statement::Import(b) => b,
[1066](#1066)            _ => panic!("expected import"),
[1067](#1067)        };
[1068](#1068)        match import.policy {
[1069](#1069)            Some(crate::ast::ReimportPolicy::FieldPriority(config)) => {

[1071](#1071)                assert_eq!(config.time, crate::ast::FieldStrategy::Wikidata);
[1072](#1072)                assert_eq!(config.tags, crate::ast::FieldStrategy::Merge);
[1073](#1073)            }
[1074](#1074)            other => panic!("expected FieldPriority, got {:?}", other),
[1075](#1075)        }
[1076](#1076)    }

[1233](#1233)    #[test]
[1234](#1234)    fn parse_time_value_accessors() {
[1235](#1235)        let d = ast::TimeValue::Date(1969, 7, 20);
[1236](#1236)        assert_eq!(d.year(), 1969);
[1237](#1237)        assert_eq!(d.month(), Some(7));
[1238](#1238)        assert_eq!(d.day(), Some(20));
[1239](#1239)
[1240](#1240)        let m = ast::TimeValue::YearMonth(1939, 9);
[1241](#1241)        assert_eq!(m.year(), 1939);
[1242](#1242)        assert_eq!(m.month(), Some(9));
[1243](#1243)        assert_eq!(m.day(), None);
[1244](#1244)
[1245](#1245)        let y = ast::TimeValue::Year(-206);
[1246](#1246)        assert_eq!(y.year(), -206);
[1247](#1247)        assert_eq!(y.month(), None);
[1248](#1248)        assert_eq!(y.day(), None);
[1249](#1249)    }

[1251](#1251)    #[test]
[1252](#1252)    fn parse_time_value_to_sortable_order() {
[1253](#1253)        use ast::TimeValue::*;
[1254](#1254)        assert!(Year(1939).to_sortable() < Year(1940).to_sortable());
[1255](#1255)        assert!(YearMonth(1939, 9).to_sortable() > YearMonth(1939, 8).to_sortable());
[1256](#1256)        assert!(Date(1939, 9, 1).to_sortable() > Date(1939, 8, 31).to_sortable());
[1257](#1257)        assert!(Year(1939).to_sortable() < YearMonth(1939, 1).to_sortable());
[1259](#1259)    }

[1355](#1355)
[1356](#1356)    #[test]
[1359](#1359)    fn parse_claim_expr_with_positive_offset() {
[1360](#1360)        let src = r#"
[1361](#1361)            map wd.x to span {
[1362](#1362)                lane a;
[1363](#1363)                start claim(P569).year +1;
[1364](#1364)                end claim(P570).year +30;
[1365](#1365)                label label@ja;
[1366](#1366)            }
[1367](#1367)        "#;
[1368](#1368)        let file = parse(src).expect("should parse claim_expr with positive offset");
[1369](#1369)        match &file.statements[0].node {
[1370](#1370)            ast::Statement::Map(m) => {
[1371](#1371)                let start = m
[1372](#1372)                    .props
[1373](#1373)                    .iter()
[1374](#1374)                    .find_map(|p| match p {
[1375](#1375)                        ast::MapProp::Start(e) => Some(e),
[1376](#1376)                        _ => None,
[1377](#1377)                    })
[1378](#1378)                    .expect("start present");
[1379](#1379)                assert_eq!(start.fallbacks.len(), 1);
[1380](#1380)                match &start.fallbacks[0] {
[1381](#1381)                    ast::MapFallback::Claim(c) => {
[1382](#1382)                        assert_eq!(c.claim.property, "P569");
[1383](#1383)                        assert_eq!(c.accessor.as_deref(), Some("year"));
[1384](#1384)                        assert_eq!(c.offset, Some(1));
[1385](#1385)                    }
[1386](#1386)                    _ => panic!("expected Claim"),
[1387](#1387)                }
[1388](#1388)
[1389](#1389)                let end = m
[1390](#1390)                    .props
[1391](#1391)                    .iter()
[1392](#1392)                    .find_map(|p| match p {
[1393](#1393)                        ast::MapProp::End(e) => Some(e),
[1394](#1394)                        _ => None,
[1395](#1395)                    })
[1396](#1396)                    .expect("end present");
[1397](#1397)                match &end.fallbacks[0] {
[1398](#1398)                    ast::MapFallback::Claim(c) => assert_eq!(c.offset, Some(30)),
[1399](#1399)                    _ => panic!("expected Claim"),
[1400](#1400)                }
[1401](#1401)            }
[1402](#1402)            _ => panic!("expected Map"),
[1403](#1403)        }
[1404](#1404)    }

[1513](#1513)                    }
[1514](#1514)                    _ => panic!("expected Claim"),

[1527](#1527)                start claim(P569).year ?? 9999;
[1528](#1528)                end claim(P570).year ?? -999;
[1529](#1529)                label label@ja;
[1530](#1530)            }
[1531](#1531)        "#;
[1532](#1532)        let file = parse(src).unwrap();
[1533](#1533)        match &file.statements[0].node {

[1538](#1538)                    .find_map(|p| match p {
[1539](#1539)                        ast::MapProp::Start(e) => Some(e),

[1541](#1541)                    })

[1548](#1548)                    }
[1549](#1549)                    _ => panic!("expected Claim"),
[1550](#1550)                }
[1551](#1551)                match &start.fallbacks[1] {

[1556](#1556)                let end = m
[1557](#1557)                    .props

[1566](#1566)                    _ => panic!("expected Literal"),
[1567](#1567)                }
[1568](#1568)            }
[1569](#1569)            _ => panic!("expected Map"),
[1570](#1570)        }
[1571](#1571)    }

[1665](#1665)    calendar proleptic_gregorian;
[1666](#1666)}
[1667](#1667)"#;
[1668](#1668)        match parse(src) {
[1670](#1670)            Err(e @ error::ParseError::InvalidMonth { .. }) => {
[1671](#1671)                let loc = e.source_location(src);

[1674](#1674)                let loc = loc.unwrap();
[1675](#1675)                assert!(loc.line >= 1, "line は 1-based で 1 以上");
[1676](#1676)                assert!(loc.col >= 1, "col は 1-based で 1 以上");
[1677](#1677)            }
[1678](#1678)            Err(e @ error::ParseError::Syntax(_)) => {
[1680](#1680)                let loc = e.source_location(src);
[1681](#1681)                assert!(loc.is_some(), "Syntax error も source_location を返す");
[1682](#1682)            }
[1683](#1683)            Ok(_) => {
[1684](#1684)                }
[1686](#1686)            Err(other) => panic!("unexpected error: {:?}", other),
[1687](#1687)        }
[1688](#1688)    }

[1768](#1768)    fn parse_diagnostic_syntax_error_has_source_span() {
[1769](#1769)        let src = "@@@";
[1770](#1770)        let err = parse(src).unwrap_err();
[1771](#1771)        let diag = error::ParseDiagnostic::from_parse_error(&err, src, "test.tdsl");
[1772](#1772)        assert!(
[1774](#1774)            diag.span().is_some(),
[1775](#1775)            "Syntax エラーは SourceSpan を持つべき"
[1776](#1776)        );
[1777](#1777)        let span = diag.span().unwrap();
[1778](#1778)        assert!(
[1780](#1780)            span.offset() <= src.len(),
[1781](#1781)            "offset {} はソース長 {} 以内であるべき",
[1782](#1782)            span.offset(),
[1783](#1783)            src.len()
[1784](#1784)        );
[1785](#1785)        assert!(!span.is_empty(), "len は 1 以上であるべき");
[1787](#1787)    }

[1891](#1891)                _ => None,
[1892](#1892)            })
[1893](#1893)            .expect("end present");
[1894](#1894)
[1895](#1895)        match &end.fallbacks[0] {
[1896](#1896)            ast::MapFallback::Claim(c) => {
[1897](#1897)                assert_eq!(c.claim.property, "P39");
[1898](#1898)                assert_eq!(c.qualifier.as_deref(), Some("P582"));
[1899](#1899)                assert_eq!(c.accessor.as_deref(), Some("year"));
[1900](#1900)            }
[1901](#1901)            _ => panic!("expected Claim"),
[1902](#1902)        }
[1903](#1903)    }
[1904](#1904)
[1905](#1905)    #[test]
[1906](#1906)    fn parse_map_expand() {
[1907](#1907)        let src = r#"
[1909](#1909)            timeline "test" {}
[1910](#1910)            import wd as w { entity Q1; }
[1911](#1911)            map wd.person to span {
[1912](#1912)                lane x;
[1913](#1913)                expand claim(P39);
[1914](#1914)                start claim(P39).qualifier(P580).year;
[1915](#1915)                end   claim(P39).qualifier(P582).year;
[1916](#1916)                label label@ja;
[1917](#1917)            }
[1918](#1918)        "#;
[1919](#1919)        let file = parse(src).unwrap();
[1920](#1920)        let map = match &file.statements[2].node {
[1921](#1921)            ast::Statement::Map(m) => m,
[1922](#1922)            _ => panic!("expected Map"),
[1923](#1923)        };
[1924](#1924)
[1925](#1925)        let expand = map
[1926](#1926)            .props
[1927](#1927)            .iter()
[1928](#1928)            .find_map(|p| match p {
[1929](#1929)                ast::MapProp::Expand(call) => Some(call),
[1930](#1930)                _ => None,
[1931](#1931)            })
[1932](#1932)            .expect("expand prop present");
[1933](#1933)
[1934](#1934)        assert_eq!(expand.property, "P39");
[1935](#1935)    }
[1936](#1936)
[1937](#1937)    #[test]

# ParseDiagnostic in tdsl_parser::error - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tdsl-parser/1.23.0/tdsl_parser/error/struct.ParseDiagnostic.html

`pub struct ParseDiagnostic { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

miette の fancy レポート（キャレット付きスニペット）を生成するための診断ラッパー。

CLI 層でのみ使用する。ライブラリ API では `ParseError` を直接返す。
`source` テキストを添付することで miette がキャレット行を表示できる。

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/tdsl_parser/error.rs.html#53-71)#### pub fn [from_parse_error](https://docs.rs#method.from_parse_error)(err: &[ParseError](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html), src: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), filename: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/tdsl_parser/error.rs.html#53-71)

#### pub fn [from_parse_error](https://docs.rs#method.from_parse_error)(err: &[ParseError](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html), src: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), filename: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> Self

`ParseError` と DSL ソース文字列からキャレット付き診断を構築する。

- `Syntax`variant: pest の- `variant.message()`から簡潔な説明文のみを取得する。 位置・スニペットは miette のキャレット描画に委ねる（pest の整形文字列は使わない）。
- バイトオフセット variant（`InvalidInt`等）:`location`フィールドの`"start:end"`文字列を使う。
- 位置情報のない variant（`UnknownPolicy`等）: スパンなしで表示する。

#### fn [color](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.color)<Color>(&self, color: Color) -> [FgDynColorDisplay](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/struct.FgDynColorDisplay.html)<'_, Color, Self>

Set the foreground color at runtime. Only use if you do not know which color will be used at
compile-time. If the color is constant, use either

[or a color-specific method, such as](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.fg)`OwoColorize::fg`[,](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.green)`OwoColorize::green`[Read more](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.color)[Source](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/owo_colors/lib.rs.html#415)[§](https://docs.rs#method.on_color)#### fn [on_color](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.on_color)<Color>(&self, color: Color) -> [BgDynColorDisplay](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/struct.BgDynColorDisplay.html)<'_, Color, Self>

#### fn [on_color](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.on_color)<Color>(&self, color: Color) -> [BgDynColorDisplay](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/struct.BgDynColorDisplay.html)<'_, Color, Self>

compile-time. If the color is constant, use either

[or a color-specific method, such as](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.bg)`OwoColorize::bg`[,](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.on_yellow)`OwoColorize::on_yellow`[Read more](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.on_color)[Source](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/owo_colors/lib.rs.html#422-424)[§](https://docs.rs#method.fg_rgb)#### fn [fg_rgb](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.fg_rgb)<const R: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html), const G: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html), const B: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>(

#### fn [fg_rgb](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.fg_rgb)<const R: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html), const G: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html), const B: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>(
    &self,

Set the background color to a specific RGB value.

Sets the foreground color to an RGB value.

# byte_offset_to_line_col in tdsl_parser::error - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tdsl-parser/1.23.0/tdsl_parser/error/fn.byte_offset_to_line_col.html

## Expand description

バイトオフセットを 1-based の (line, col) に変換する。

pest の span はバイト単位かつ char 境界に揃っているため `src` のスライスは安全。
LSP など、AST ノードの `Span`（バイトオフセット）から行・列を求める用途でも再利用する。

---

# tdsl_parser::error - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tdsl-parser/1.23.0/tdsl_parser/error/index.html

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseDiagnostic.html)- Diagnostic
- miette の fancy レポート（キャレット付きスニペット）を生成するための診断ラッパー。
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseErrorLoc.html)- Error - Loc
- DSL ソース内の位置情報（1-based 行番号・列番号）。 LSP や WASM バインディングで診断位置を返すために使用する。

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

[Source](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/owo_colors/lib.rs.html#399)[§](https://docs.rs#method.color)#### fn [color](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.color)<Color>(&self, color: Color) -> [FgDynColorDisplay](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/struct.FgDynColorDisplay.html)<'_, Color, Self>

[Source](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/owo_colors/lib.rs.html#399)

[§](https://docs.rs#method.color)

#### fn [color](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.color)<Color>(&self, color: Color) -> [FgDynColorDisplay](https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/owo_colors/struct.FgDynColorDisplay.html)<'_, Color, Self>

Set the foreground color at runtime. Only use if you do not know which color will be used at
compile-time. If the color is constant, use either

`statements: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Spanned](https://docs.rs/struct.Spanned.html)<[Statement](https://docs.rs/enum.Statement.html)>>[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.comments)

`comments: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Spanned](https://docs.rs/struct.Spanned.html)<[Comment](https://docs.rs/struct.Comment.html)>>元ソースに含まれていたコメント（出現順、byte span 付き）。

コメントは [ crate::parse](https://docs.rs/fn.parse.html) 時に専用パスで収集され、文（statement）とは独立に
保持される。lowering では一切参照されないため IR には影響しない（#362 / #473）。
フォーマッタ（

[）はこの情報を使ってコメントを再 emit する。](https://docs.rs/format/fn.format_file.html)

compile-time. If the color is constant, use either

# aes_gcm - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/aes-gcm/^0.10/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#rustcrypto-aes-gcm)RustCrypto: AES-GCM

Pure Rust implementation of the AES-GCM
[Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Authenticated_encryption) cipher.

[§](https://docs.rs#security-notes)Security Notes

This crate has received one [security audit by NCC Group](https://research.nccgroup.com/2020/02/26/public-report-rustcrypto-aes-gcm-and-chacha20poly1305-implementation-review/), with no significant
findings. We would like to thank [MobileCoin](https://www.mobilecoin.com/) for funding the audit.

All implementations contained in the crate are designed to execute in constant time, either by relying on hardware intrinsics (i.e. AES-NI and CLMUL on x86/x86_64), or using a portable implementation which is only constant time on processors which implement constant-time multiplication.

It is not suitable for use on processors with a variable-time multiplication operation (e.g. short circuit on multiply-by-zero / multiply-by-one, such as certain 32-bit PowerPC CPUs and some non-ARM microcontrollers).

[§](https://docs.rs#license)License

Licensed under either of:

at your option.

[§](https://docs.rs#contribution)Contribution

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in the work by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

Simple usage (allocating, no associated data):

```
use aes_gcm::{
    aead::{Aead, AeadCore, KeyInit, OsRng},
    Aes256Gcm, Nonce, Key // Or `Aes128Gcm`
};
// The encryption key can be generated randomly:
let key = Aes256Gcm::generate_key(OsRng);
// Transformed from a byte array:
let key: &[u8; 32] = &[42; 32];
let key: &Key<Aes256Gcm> = key.into();
// Note that you can get byte array from slice using the `TryInto` trait:
let key: &[u8] = &[42; 32];
let key: [u8; 32] = key.try_into()?;
// Alternatively, the key can be transformed directly from a byte slice
// (panicks on length mismatch):
let key = Key::<Aes256Gcm>::from_slice(key);
let cipher = Aes256Gcm::new(&key);
let nonce = Aes256Gcm::generate_nonce(&mut OsRng); // 96-bits; unique per message
let ciphertext = cipher.encrypt(&nonce, b"plaintext message".as_ref())?;
let plaintext = cipher.decrypt(&nonce, ciphertext.as_ref())?;
assert_eq!(&plaintext, b"plaintext message");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#in-place-usage-eliminates-alloc-requirement)In-place Usage (eliminates `alloc` requirement)

This crate has an optional `alloc` feature which can be disabled in e.g.
microcontroller environments that don’t have a heap.

The [ AeadInPlace::encrypt_in_place](https://docs.rs/trait.AeadInPlace.html#method.encrypt_in_place) and

[methods accept any type that impls the](https://docs.rs/trait.AeadInPlace.html#method.decrypt_in_place)

`AeadInPlace::decrypt_in_place`[trait which contains the plaintext for encryption or ciphertext for decryption.](https://docs.rs/aead/0.5.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/aead/trait.Buffer.html)

`aead::Buffer`Note that if you enable the `heapless` feature of this crate,
you will receive an impl of [ aead::Buffer](https://docs.rs/aead/0.5.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/aead/trait.Buffer.html) for

`heapless::Vec`
(re-exported from the [crate as](https://docs.rs/aead/0.5.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/aead/index.html)

`aead`[), which can then be passed as the](https://docs.rs/heapless/0.7.17/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/heapless/vec/struct.Vec.html)

`aead::heapless::Vec``buffer` parameter to the in-place encrypt
and decrypt methods:```
use aes_gcm::{
    aead::{AeadCore, AeadInPlace, KeyInit, OsRng, heapless::Vec},
    Aes256Gcm, Nonce, // Or `Aes128Gcm`
};
let key = Aes256Gcm::generate_key(&mut OsRng);
let cipher = Aes256Gcm::new(&key);
let nonce = Aes256Gcm::generate_nonce(&mut OsRng); // 96-bits; unique per message
let mut buffer: Vec<u8, 128> = Vec::new(); // Note: buffer needs 16-bytes overhead for auth tag
buffer.extend_from_slice(b"plaintext message");
// Encrypt `buffer` in-place, replacing the plaintext contents with ciphertext
cipher.encrypt_in_place(&nonce, b"", &mut buffer)?;
// `buffer` now contains the message ciphertext
assert_ne!(&buffer, b"plaintext message");
// Decrypt `buffer` in-place, replacing its ciphertext context with the original plaintext
cipher.decrypt_in_place(&nonce, b"", &mut buffer)?;
assert_eq!(&buffer, b"plaintext message");
```
Similarly, enabling the `arrayvec` feature of this crate will provide an impl of
[ aead::Buffer](https://docs.rs/aead/0.5.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/aead/trait.Buffer.html) for

`arrayvec::ArrayVec` (re-exported from the [crate as](https://docs.rs/aead/0.5.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/aead/index.html)

`aead`[).](https://docs.rs/arrayvec/0.7.6/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/arrayvec/arrayvec/struct.ArrayVec.html)

`aead::arrayvec::ArrayVec`## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

# base64 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/base64/^0.22/

## Expand description

Correct, fast, and configurable [base64](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Base64) decoding and encoding. Base64
transports binary data efficiently in contexts where only plain text is
allowed.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

Use an [ Engine](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html) to decode or encode base64, configured with the base64
alphabet and padding behavior best suited to your application.

[§](https://docs.rs#engine-setup)Engine setup

There is more than one way to encode a stream of bytes as “base64”.
Different applications use different encoding
[alphabets](https://docs.rs/alphabet/struct.Alphabet.html) and
[padding behaviors](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/struct.GeneralPurposeConfig.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#encoding-alphabet)Encoding alphabet

Almost all base64 [alphabets](https://docs.rs/alphabet/struct.Alphabet.html) use `A-Z`, `a-z`, and
`0-9`, which gives nearly 64 characters (26 + 26 + 10 = 62), but they differ
in their choice of their final 2.

Most applications use the [standard](https://docs.rs/alphabet/constant.STANDARD.html) alphabet specified
in [RFC 4648](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4648#section-4).  If that’s all you need, you can get started
quickly by using the pre-configured
[ STANDARD](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/constant.STANDARD.html) engine, which is also available
in the

[module as shown here, if you prefer a minimal](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)

`prelude``use`
footprint.```
use base64::prelude::*;
assert_eq!(BASE64_STANDARD.decode(b"+uwgVQA=")?, b"\xFA\xEC\x20\x55\0");
assert_eq!(BASE64_STANDARD.encode(b"\xFF\xEC\x20\x55\0"), "/+wgVQA=");
```
Other common alphabets are available in the [ alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/index.html) module.

[§](https://docs.rs#url-safe-alphabet)URL-safe alphabet

The standard alphabet uses `+` and `/` as its two non-alphanumeric tokens,
which cannot be safely used in URL’s without encoding them as `%2B` and
`%2F`.

To avoid that, some applications use a [“URL-safe” alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/constant.URL_SAFE.html),
which uses `-` and `_` instead. To use that alternative alphabet, use the
[ URL_SAFE](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/constant.URL_SAFE.html) engine. This example doesn’t
use

[to show what a more explicit](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)

`prelude``use` would look like.```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE, Engine as _};
assert_eq!(URL_SAFE.decode(b"-uwgVQA=")?, b"\xFA\xEC\x20\x55\0");
assert_eq!(URL_SAFE.encode(b"\xFF\xEC\x20\x55\0"), "_-wgVQA=");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#padding-characters)Padding characters

Each base64 character represents 6 bits (2⁶ = 64) of the original binary data, and every 3 bytes of input binary data will encode to 4 base64 characters (8 bits × 3 = 6 bits × 4 = 24 bits).

When the input is not an even multiple of 3 bytes in length, [canonical](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4648#section-3.5)
base64 encoders insert padding characters at the end, so that the output
length is always a multiple of 4:

```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD, Engine as _};
assert_eq!(STANDARD.encode(b""),    "");
assert_eq!(STANDARD.encode(b"f"),   "Zg==");
assert_eq!(STANDARD.encode(b"fo"),  "Zm8=");
assert_eq!(STANDARD.encode(b"foo"), "Zm9v");
```
Canonical encoding ensures that base64 encodings will be exactly the same,
byte-for-byte, regardless of input length. But the `=` padding characters
aren’t necessary for decoding, and they may be omitted by using a
[ NO_PAD](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/constant.NO_PAD.html) configuration:

```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD_NO_PAD, Engine as _};
assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.encode(b""),    "");
assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.encode(b"f"),   "Zg");
assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.encode(b"fo"),  "Zm8");
assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.encode(b"foo"), "Zm9v");
```
The pre-configured `NO_PAD` engines will reject inputs containing padding
`=` characters. To encode without padding and still accept padding while
decoding, create an [engine](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/struct.GeneralPurpose.html) with
that [padding mode](https://docs.rs/engine/enum.DecodePaddingMode.html).

`assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.decode(b"Zm8="), Err(base64::DecodeError::InvalidPadding));`[§](https://docs.rs#further-customization)Further customization

Decoding and encoding behavior can be customized by creating an
[engine](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/struct.GeneralPurpose.html) with an [alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/struct.Alphabet.html) and
[padding configuration](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/struct.GeneralPurposeConfig.html):

```
use base64::{engine, alphabet, Engine as _};
// bizarro-world base64: +/ as the first symbols instead of the last
let alphabet =
    alphabet::Alphabet::new("+/ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789")
    .unwrap();
// a very weird config that encodes with padding but requires no padding when decoding...?
let crazy_config = engine::GeneralPurposeConfig::new()
    .with_decode_allow_trailing_bits(true)
    .with_encode_padding(true)
    .with_decode_padding_mode(engine::DecodePaddingMode::RequireNone);
let crazy_engine = engine::GeneralPurpose::new(&alphabet, crazy_config);
let encoded = crazy_engine.encode(b"abc 123");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#memory-allocation)Memory allocation

The [decode](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html#method.decode) and [encode](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html#method.encode) engine methods
allocate memory for their results – `decode` returns a `Vec<u8>` and
`encode` returns a `String`. To instead decode or encode into a buffer that
you allocated, use one of the alternative methods:

[§](https://docs.rs#decoding)Decoding

| Method | Output | Allocates memory |
|---|---|---|
| `Engine::decode` | returns a new `Vec<u8>` | always |
| `Engine::decode_vec` | appends to provided `Vec<u8>` | if `Vec`lacks capacity |
| `Engine::decode_slice` | writes to provided `&[u8]` | never |

[§](https://docs.rs#encoding)Encoding

| Method | Output | Allocates memory |
|---|---|---|
| `Engine::encode` | returns a new `String` | always |
| `Engine::encode_string` | appends to provided `String` | if `String`lacks capacity |
| `Engine::encode_slice` | writes to provided `&[u8]` | never |

[§](https://docs.rs#input-and-output)Input and output

The `base64` crate can [decode](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html#method.decode) and
[encode](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html#method.encode) values in memory, or
[ DecoderReader](https://docs.rs/read/struct.DecoderReader.html) and

[provide streaming decoding and encoding for any](https://docs.rs/write/struct.EncoderWriter.html)

`EncoderWriter`[readable](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Read.html)or

[writable](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Write.html)byte stream.

[§](https://docs.rs#decoding-1)Decoding

```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD, read::DecoderReader};
let mut input = io::stdin();
let mut decoder = DecoderReader::new(&mut input, &STANDARD);
io::copy(&mut decoder, &mut io::stdout())?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#encoding-1)Encoding

```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD, write::EncoderWriter};
let mut output = io::stdout();
let mut encoder = EncoderWriter::new(&mut output, &STANDARD);
io::copy(&mut io::stdin(), &mut encoder)?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#display)Display

If you only need a base64 representation for implementing the
[ Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Display.html) trait, use

[:](https://docs.rs/display/struct.Base64Display.html)

`Base64Display````
use base64::{display::Base64Display, engine::general_purpose::STANDARD};
let value = Base64Display::new(b"\0\x01\x02\x03", &STANDARD);
assert_eq!("base64: AAECAw==", format!("base64: {}", value));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

If length calculations result in overflowing `usize`, a panic will result.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

# hex - Rust

[and](https://docs.rs/fn.encode.html)

`ToHex`[instead.](https://docs.rs/trait.FromHex.html)

`FromHex`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

let hex_string = hex::encode("Hello world!");
println!("{}", hex_string); // Prints "48656c6c6f20776f726c6421"
```

# hmac - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/hmac/^0.12/

## Expand description

Generic implementation of Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC).

To use it you will need a cryptographic hash function implementation which
implements the [ digest](https://docs.rs/digest) crate traits. You can find compatible crates
(e.g.

[) in the](https://docs.rs/sha2)

`sha2`[repository.](https://github.com/RustCrypto/hashes)

`RustCrypto/hashes`This crate provides two HMAC implementation [ Hmac](https://docs.rs/type.Hmac.html) and

[. The first one is a buffered wrapper around block-level](https://docs.rs/struct.SimpleHmac.html)

`SimpleHmac`[. Internally it uses efficient state representation, but works only with hash functions which expose block-level API and consume blocks eagerly (e.g. it will not work with the BLAKE2 family of hash functions). On the other hand,](https://docs.rs/struct.HmacCore.html)

`HmacCore`[is a bit less efficient memory-wise, but works with all hash functions which implement the](https://docs.rs/struct.SimpleHmac.html)

`SimpleHmac`[trait.](https://docs.rs/digest)

`Digest`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Let us demonstrate how to use HMAC using the SHA-256 hash function.

In the following examples [ Hmac](https://docs.rs/type.Hmac.html) is interchangeable with

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.SimpleHmac.html)

`SimpleHmac`To get authentication code:

```
use sha2::Sha256;
use hmac::{Hmac, Mac};
use hex_literal::hex;
// Create alias for HMAC-SHA256
type HmacSha256 = Hmac<Sha256>;
let mut mac = HmacSha256::new_from_slice(b"my secret and secure key")
    .expect("HMAC can take key of any size");
mac.update(b"input message");
// `result` has type `CtOutput` which is a thin wrapper around array of
// bytes for providing constant time equality check
let result = mac.finalize();
// To get underlying array use `into_bytes`, but be careful, since
// incorrect use of the code value may permit timing attacks which defeats
// the security provided by the `CtOutput`
let code_bytes = result.into_bytes();
let expected = hex!("
    97d2a569059bbcd8ead4444ff99071f4
    c01d005bcefe0d3567e1be628e5fdcd9
");
assert_eq!(code_bytes[..], expected[..]);
```
To verify the message:

```
let mut mac = HmacSha256::new_from_slice(b"my secret and secure key")
    .expect("HMAC can take key of any size");
mac.update(b"input message");
let code_bytes = hex!("
    97d2a569059bbcd8ead4444ff99071f4
    c01d005bcefe0d3567e1be628e5fdcd9
");
// `verify_slice` will return `Ok(())` if code is correct, `Err(MacError)` otherwise
mac.verify_slice(&code_bytes[..]).unwrap();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#block-and-input-sizes)Block and input sizes

Usually it is assumed that block size is larger than output size. Due to the generic nature of the implementation, this edge case must be handled as well to remove potential panic. This is done by truncating hash output to the hash block size if needed.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [digest](https://docs.rs/digest/0.10.7/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/digest/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Hmac](https://docs.rs/struct.HmacCore.html)- Core
- Generic core HMAC instance, which operates over blocks.
- [Simple](https://docs.rs/struct.SimpleHmac.html)- Hmac
- Simplified HMAC instance able to operate over hash functions which do not expose block-level API and hash functions which process blocks lazily (e.g. BLAKE2).

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Mac](https://docs.rs/trait.Mac.html)
- Convenience wrapper trait covering functionality of Message Authentication algorithms.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Hmac](https://docs.rs/type.Hmac.html)
- Generic HMAC instance.

# pbkdf2 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pbkdf2/^0.12/

## Expand description

This crate implements the PBKDF2 key derivation function as specified
in [RFC 2898](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2898).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

PBKDF2 is defined in terms of a keyed pseudo-random function (PRF). Most
commonly HMAC is used as this PRF. In such cases you can use [ pbkdf2_hmac](https://docs.rs/fn.pbkdf2_hmac.html)
and

[functions. The former accepts a byte slice which gets filled with generated key, while the former returns an array with generated key of requested length.](https://docs.rs/fn.pbkdf2_hmac_array.html)

`pbkdf2_hmac_array````
use hex_literal::hex;
use pbkdf2::{pbkdf2_hmac, pbkdf2_hmac_array};
use sha2::Sha256;
let password = b"password";
let salt = b"salt";
// number of iterations
let n = 600_000;
// Expected value of generated key
let expected = hex!("669cfe52482116fda1aa2cbe409b2f56c8e45637");
let mut key1 = [0u8; 20];
pbkdf2_hmac::<Sha256>(password, salt, n, &mut key1);
assert_eq!(key1, expected);
let key2 = pbkdf2_hmac_array::<Sha256, 20>(password, salt, n);
assert_eq!(key2, expected);
```
If you want to use a different PRF, then you can use [ pbkdf2](https://docs.rs/fn.pbkdf2.html)
and

[functions.](https://docs.rs/fn.pbkdf2_array.html)

`pbkdf2_array`This crates also provides the high-level password-hashing API through
the [ Pbkdf2](https://docs.rs/struct.Pbkdf2.html) struct and traits defined in the

[crate.](https://docs.rs/password-hash/0.5.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/password_hash/index.html)

`password-hash`Add the following to your crate’s `Cargo.toml` to import it:

```
[dependencies]
pbkdf2 = { version = "0.12", features = ["simple"] }
rand_core = { version = "0.6", features = ["std"] }
```
The following example demonstrates the high-level password hashing API:

```
use pbkdf2::{
    password_hash::{
        rand_core::OsRng,
        PasswordHash, PasswordHasher, PasswordVerifier, SaltString
    },
    Pbkdf2
};
let password = b"hunter42"; // Bad password; don't actually use!
let salt = SaltString::generate(&mut OsRng);
// Hash password to PHC string ($pbkdf2-sha256$...)
let password_hash = Pbkdf2.hash_password(password, &salt)?.to_string();
// Verify password against PHC string
let parsed_hash = PasswordHash::new(&password_hash)?;
assert!(Pbkdf2.verify_password(password, &parsed_hash).is_ok());
```

- `pub use`- [hmac](https://docs.rs/hmac/0.12.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hmac/index.html);- `hmac`

- PBKDF2 params

- PBKDF2 variants.
